To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) ethanol elicits apoptotically programmed cell death of fetal cortical neurons, (ii) this process is enhanced in low‐glutathione (G‐SH) neurons, (iii) the low‐G‐SH neurons have a higher content of 4hydroxynonenale (4‐HN), (iv) ethanol increases the 4‐HN content, and (v) the 4‐HNE content is elevated in the low G‐SH neurons.
the sensitivity of fetal cortical neurons to apoptotic cell death induced by ethanol is mediated, at least in part, by glutathione content.
glutathione (a cellular antioxidant) levels are a major factor that influences the vulnerability of cultured neurons to ethanol‐mediation of oxidative stress and subsequent apoptotic cell death.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how alcohol affects the developing nervous system.
the effects of prenatal exposure to ethanol on the developing brain.
how ethanol elicits damage to specific neuronal populations within the developing brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glutathione content is a potential mediator of neuronal vulnerability to ethanol‐inducible apoptosis.
the differences in ethanol‐mediated apoptotic responses in specific neuronal populations may reflect a heterogeneity in neuronal GSH content.
the differences in ethanol‐mediated proapoptotic effects within specific neuron populations may reflect a heterogeneity in the content of the antioxidant, glutathione (see Fig. 2).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GSH content is a potential mediator of ethanol‐induced apoptotic death in cultured fetal cortical neurons.

GSH content may be a potential mediator of ethanol‐induced apoptotic cell death in the fetal brain, and that GABAergic neurons may be more vulnerable to ethanol‐inducible oxidative stress and apoptosis due to their low GSH content.
the vulnerability of neurons to ethanol‐mediates apoptosis is mediated by the cellular content of glutathione.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glutathione (the most abundant antioxidant in the brain and body), is a major factor in the vulnerability of the developing brain to ethanol.

glutathione (a small protein that is present in all mammalian cells) may play a critical role in determining which brain cell populations are most vulnerable to ethanol‐inducible oxidative stress and apoptosis.
the vulnerability of neurons to ethanol‐mediation of apoptosis is a reflection of the GSH content of the cell.
